findings.reason: the section's justification and its test arms rest on a divergence that does not exist at the plan's base, so the node as written would chase a behavioural fault the code no longer has.
findings.text: §22 states "the review records one revision on which they disagree: an all-zero `commits:` value, refused by the audit's copy and accepted by promotion's", but both `_commit_resolves_in` definitions delegate to the same `reckon.crew.recovery._resolve_commit` (`reckon/crew/reports.py:2082-2086` returns `bool(_resolve_commit(root, revision))`; `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py:383-385` returns `_commit_canonical_id(root, revision) is not None`, and `_commit_canonical_id` at `:380` is `_resolve_commit(root, revision) or None`), and measuring both against `/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon` gives `False` for the all-zero hash and `True` for a real commit (head `d9a2bff5a`) — the two agree, so no revision makes them answer differently and the collapse is a pure de-duplication, the divergence having been eliminated on 2026-10-05 by `513d1cc36` ("refactor(crew): resolve commit citations through one bounded lookup"), which repointed the `reports.py` copy at `_resolve_commit`

findings.reason: a control that cannot fail leaves the node's gate unable to show its change does anything; the health review's own treatment names a control that can fail (removing the single definition turns the citation tests red) and §22 should adopt that instead.
findings.text: §22's declared negative control ("re-add the `reports.py` copy delegating to `_resolve_commit`, and the test then shows the two readers disagreeing on at least one revision") cannot go red, because `reckon/crew/reports.py:2082-2086` already delegates to `_resolve_commit`, so the "re-added" copy is byte-equivalent to the one it replaces and the three arms (a real commit both accept, an all-zero hash both refuse, an unknown hash both refuse) all pass on the unfixed base
